chunks: One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: Do not wash from the well in which the used water of the bathhouse gathers, for therein is the washing of the son of adultery, and he is not clean up to seven fathers; and therein is the washing of the Nasibi, and he is the worse of the two. Indeed, Allah did not create a creature more evil than the dog, and the Nasibi is lighter (more acceptable) to Allah than the dog.

I said: Inform me about the water of the bathhouse; the one with major impurity, the child, the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian wash from it. He said: Indeed, the water of the bathhouse is like the water of the river; some of it purifies the other.

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: The Nasibi (one opposed to the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: The one with major ritual impurity
key_terms.يُطَهِّرُ بَعْضُهُ بَعْضاً: Some of it purifies the other

ai.seo_question: Is the water in a bathhouse considered pure for ritual washing according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of water purity by distinguishing between the impurity of the source (the well) and the self-purifying nature of the flowing water, likening it to a river. It further enriches Shia theological discourse by elevating the status of the 'Nasibi' (those opposed to the Imams) above the dog, a common symbol of impurity, to highlight the severity of their spiritual state. The ruling on bathhouse water being pure for all sects, including Jews and Christians, underscores the concept of external ritual cleanliness regardless of internal belief.

en.hubeali:
One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad Bin Al Qasim, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Do not wash from the well wherein the used water of the bathhouse gathers to, for therein is the washing of the son of adultery (bastard), and he is not clean up to seven fathers (generations); and therein has washed the Hostile One (Nasibi), and he is more evil of the two. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> did not Create a creature more evil than the dog, and the Hostile One (Nasibi) is lower to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> than the dog’.

I said, ‘Inform me about the water of the bathhouse. From it washes the one with sexual impurity, and the children, and the Jews, and the Christians, and the Magians’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The water of the bathhouse is like the water of the river. Some of it purifies the other’.
en.sarwar: 1. Certain persons of our people have narrated from ibn Jumhur from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Do not take Ghusl (bath) from a well in which water from bath houses accumulate, because in it there is water which is used by one born out of wedlock and it does not become clean for seven generations. In it there is water used by one hostile to ’A’immah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam. One who is hostile to ’A’immah, Alayhim al-Salam, is the worse than the two others. Allah has not created a creature more evil than the dog but one hostile to ’A’immah is more worthless than a dog.’

I then asked him (the Imam) about the water of bathhouses from which one involved in sexual activities, children, Jews, Christians and Zoroastrians take Ghusl (bath). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is like canals in which one part of water cleanses the other part.’”
